# lpass-wrap

> A typed Python wrapper around the LastPass CLI (`lpass`) for reading and
> writing vault items without exposing secrets in process argument lists.
> Secrets are always passed to `lpass` over stdin; secret-bearing model fields
> are pydantic `SecretStr` so they cannot leak into logs or tracebacks by
> accident; every subprocess call is bounded by a timeout. It also exposes the
> sync diagnostics that `lpass`'s background upload queue makes necessary —
> without them, a write-then-check script silently creates duplicate vault
> entries. Ships a console script that serves Ansible Vault passwords via
> `vault_identity_list`. Python 3.10+, Apache-2.0.

Fastest safe path to first success: install from git, call
`LpassClient(username=...)`, then `get_password("Some/Item")`. Reads are safe
and idempotent; do writes with `upsert()` and always follow them with
`assert_sync_clean()`.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): Install, quick start, full API reference for
  `LpassClient` and `LpassItem`, the exception hierarchy, sync diagnostics, the
  Ansible vault-password script, and logging setup. Read this first.
- [README — AI-agent quickstart](README.md#ai-agent-quickstart): The five rules
  that matter when generating code against this library. Read before writing
  any consumer code.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): Threat model — what the library protects against
  (secrets in argv, secrets in logs, unbounded network waits) and what it
  explicitly does not (an unlocked vault, a compromised local environment,
  secrets in memory, explicitly unwrapped values). Read before assuming a
  security property.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): Version history. 0.2.0 carries two breaking
  changes — `SecretStr` fields and subprocess timeouts — each with migration
  notes. Read when upgrading.

## Contributing

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Operational facts for working *on* the repo — setup,
  the five gates, file layout, and eight rules that will trip you up. Read
  before editing any source file.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): Dev setup, code conventions, test and
  documentation expectations, commit format.

## Reference

- [Usage notes](.claude/skills/lpass-wrap-usage/SKILL.md): Method-by-method
  guidance for consumers — which methods sync and which read a stale cache, why
  `upsert` is the right default, catching `LpassSyncError`, and an Ansible task
  pattern for verifying sync.
- [Internals and lpass CLI behaviour](.claude/skills/lpass-wrap-dev/SKILL.md):
  `$LPASS_HOME` resolution order, the upload-queue and duplicate-entry
  mechanism, `lpass` CLI log levels, and why create/update is a single
  `lpass edit` call. Read when debugging sync failures or duplicate items.

## Optional

- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml): Dependencies, tool configuration, and the
  console-script entry point. Note that dev dependencies are PEP 735
  `[dependency-groups]`, not extras — use `uv sync`, not `pip install -e ".[dev]"`.
- [tests/test_client.py](tests/test_client.py): Mocking patterns for every
  `lpass` subprocess call. Copy these rather than inventing new ones.
